competitors.name: KnowBe4
competitors.entry_point: AIDA suite of autonomous AI agents inside phishing simulation setup
competitors.setup_friction: Admin specifies parameters — difficulty level and/or NIST Phish Scale Social Engineering Indicators — rather than a free-text prompt
core_flow: Admin sets simulation parameters (difficulty, Social Engineering Indicators)
Template Generation Agent autonomously constructs a realistic template reflecting current attack vectors
Recommended Landing Pages Agent auto-suggests a matching landing page
Callback Template Generation Agent handles callback-phishing templates as a separate specialized path
competitors.trust_model: Not documented publicly; no explicit review/edit step described between generation and deployment
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: Framed as reducing admin workflows 'from hours to seconds' via autonomous agents (AIDA Orchestration)
competitors.ai_personalization: Observed — generative template creation anchored to NIST Phish Scale framework indicators
competitors.risk_score_surface: Not documented in scope of pages reviewed
competitors.remediation_path: Not documented in scope of pages reviewed
competitors.source_notes: Sourced from knowbe4.com/products/aida/agents (fetched directly). support.knowbe4.com AIDA setup article returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. No hands-on trial.

competitors.name: Hoxhunt
competitors.setup_friction: Minimal author input — difficulty is largely algorithmic and per-user rather than author-selected per template
core_flow: Algorithm selects simulation difficulty per user (four-tier scale, easy to expert)
'Spicy Mode' adds further challenge for advanced users
AI generates simulation content matching current attack sophistication
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: Adaptive per-user targeting removes manual re-selection of difficulty over time
competitors.ai_personalization: Observed — AI-generated content plus per-user adaptive difficulty
competitors.risk_score_surface: Implied via performance-based adaptive difficulty, not explicitly detailed
competitors.remediation_path: Not documented in scope of pages reviewed
competitors.source_notes: Sourced from hoxhunt.com/blog/best-phishing-simulation-tools and general search summaries. Note: a Hoxhunt-authored blog post comparing competitors was found to mischaracterize KnowBe4 as non-generative, contradicting KnowBe4's own product pages — flagged as vendor-biased and down-weighted where it concerns other vendors, not Hoxhunt itself.

competitors.name: Cofense
competitors.entry_point: Reporter-button and Triage ecosystem; real reported emails feed into simulation content via analyst review
competitors.setup_friction: Real-email-to-simulation path is analyst-mediated (report to Cofense Triage, then converted), not a direct self-serve upload by the requesting admin
core_flow: Employee reports a suspicious email via Reporter button
Email routes to Cofense Triage for analyst review
Verified/reported emails can be converted into simulation content
Admins otherwise select from a large pre-built template library (1,500+ templates, 36 languages) with automation for scheduling and smart suggestions
competitors.trust_model: Analyst-mediated review before real content becomes simulation content — a more conservative posture toward real-email content than a self-serve upload
competitors.repeat_use_efficiency: Smart suggestions based on historical simulation results and active threats; 12-month campaign automation
competitors.ai_personalization: Not clearly generative — primarily library- and automation-driven rather than AI-authored content synthesis
competitors.risk_score_surface: Not documented in scope of pages reviewed
competitors.remediation_path: Reporter/Triage closed loop supports remediation across other inboxes once a real phish is confirmed
competitors.source_notes: No source explicitly documents a named 'upload an email, get a template' feature; the real-email-to-simulation path is inferred from descriptions of the Reporter/Triage ecosystem and should be treated as a moderate-confidence inference, not a confirmed feature match.

observed_patterns: Framework-anchored difficulty controls (KnowBe4's NIST Phish Scale Social Engineering Indicators) make sophistication levels explainable rather than opaque
Auto-pairing complementary generated assets (KnowBe4's landing-page agent alongside template agent)
Using historical simulation results and active-threat data to inform what content to generate or suggest next (Cofense)
anti_patterns: No publicly documented review/edit gate before a generated template is used (KnowBe4) — a trust risk if true
Analyst-mediated-only pipeline for real-email-sourced content (Cofense) — safer but reintroduces the central-team dependency Dune's PRD is trying to remove
Fully opaque, per-user algorithmic difficulty with no per-template author control (Hoxhunt) — not a fit for Dune's analyst-authored difficulty model
differentiation_opportunities: Self-serve, ~10-second real-email-to-template flow has no documented competitor equivalent — Cofense's closest analog is analyst-mediated and slower
Naming what each difficulty tier actually changes (echoing the PRD's Easy/Medium/Hard behavior table) out-differentiates opaque labels used elsewhere
Explicit WYSIWYG edit + desktop/mobile preview step can be positioned as a deliberate trust/quality checkpoint, since competitors don't publicly describe an equivalent review step
design_implications: Surface what each difficulty tier changes directly in the UI rather than presenting unexplained Easy/Medium/Hard labels
Design the Copy an Email upload flow from Dune's own conventions (e.g., aep-library-adjacent patterns) since no competitor offers a directly comparable self-serve real-email-upload flow to reference
Frame the WYSIWYG edit/preview step as a named, deliberate checkpoint rather than an incidental post-generation editor

Treat the still-unresolved retention/handling question for uploaded .eml content as a competitive as well as compliance question, given Cofense's more conservative analyst-mediated posture toward real-email content
confidence_notes: Sourced from official vendor marketing/product pages and search-aggregated summaries, not hands-on product trials
KnowBe4 AIDA setup support article (support.knowbe4.com) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read directly; findings rely on the aida/agents product page only
A Hoxhunt-authored competitor-comparison blog was identified as vendor-biased regarding its characterization of KnowBe4 and was down-weighted accordingly
Cofense's real-email-to-template capability is a moderate-confidence inference from Reporter/Triage ecosystem descriptions, not a confirmed named feature
No competitor source addressed image-embedded redaction, workspace isolation, or RBAC granularity in enough detail for direct comparison on those dimensions
